statement: ts_rs's #[ts(export, export_to = "...")] per-type attribute and TS::export_all_to(out_dir) called separately compose additively rather than one overriding the other: setting export_to on a type AND calling export_all_to(dir) produced a nested dir/export_to/ path instead of just dir/. Removing the per-type #[ts(export_to = ...)] attribute entirely and driving everything through one export_all_to(out_dir) call in a shared ts_export module (called by both the export bin and the drift test) is the correct pattern for a committed-bindings pipeline.
why: crates/enforcer-ui/src/payload.rs originally had #[ts(export, export_to = "../frontend/src/bindings/")] on UiFindingRow/UiReportPayload; running the export bin produced crates/enforcer-ui/frontend/src/frontend/src/bindings/*.ts (doubled path) instead of crates/enforcer-ui/frontend/src/bindings/*.ts.
howToApply: For any future ts_rs export pipeline (arc-24 or a Track G pack extending it), do not put #[ts(export_to = ...)] on individual domain/DTO types; instead call Type::export_all_to(out_dir) explicitly from one pipeline function per type-set, and let that same out_dir also be reused by the drift test's fresh-export scratch comparison.

statement: The no-naked-domain-strings check's TS-1.3 rule (naked domain string alias forbidden) fires on ts_rs-generated .ts bindings (e.g. export type RuleId = string; in the generated RelPath.ts/RuleId.ts) because ts_rs erases a Rust branded newtype to its serde wire representation when emitting TypeScript -- that is the correct/expected shape for a DERIVED binding, not the hand-written naked-string alias TS-1.3 is meant to catch. The generated-artifacts check already recognizes these same files as generated and passes clean on them, so the fix pattern exists (recognize the ts-rs generated-file header) but TS-1.3 itself does not yet apply it.
why: arc-24 is the first crate in the workspace to emit ts_rs-derived .ts output; every future arc-24 export and every Track G feature pack (g01..g08) landing UI-facing types will trip this same false positive going forward until the TS-1.3 rule/validator (likely enforcer-lang-ts, arc-07) is taught to skip generated bindings the same way generated-artifacts already does.
howToApply: Do not attempt to work around this inside enforcer-ui (out of its owns: scope, and per-type attribute tricks don't fix a checker-side gap). File/track a fix against the TS-1.3 rule/validator itself (spawned as task_d323e7a1 in this session) rather than re-litigating it per Track-G pack.

statement: The MCP coordination_claim/coordination_mail tools refused to write with a stale-server error the entire session (mcpFreshness.stale=true, a package.json byte-length delta), and the CLI fallback (node scripts/rust-rules.mjs coordination claim ...) also failed with ENOENT on .ledger/ocentra-parent/identity/node.json. Both the primary MCP path and its own documented fallback were unavailable for lane claim/mail during this run.
why: Per the arc-24 dispatch protocol, hub coordination is best-effort ("log attempts, proceed") specifically to tolerate exactly this kind of hub unavailability without blocking a worker's actual crate-building work.
howToApply: When both ocentra_enforcer_coordination_* MCP tools AND their CLI fallback (scripts/rust-rules.mjs coordination ...) fail, log the attempt/error once, do not retry in a loop, and proceed with file-level work using the workpack's owns: globs as the de facto claim boundary (they are already disjoint by plan construction).
